headline: Bitcoin has slipped back to about $64,000 after a $2B weekend wipe-out of leveraged bets, its sixth straight weekly loss, with fear at extreme levels ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's remarks at noon ET.

market.asOf: Read at about 12:00 UTC Mon 16 Nov (19:00 Bangkok) from CoinGecko's coin pages. The 24-hour change is left out because the sources disagree on direction: CoinGecko showed BTC down 1.0%, ETH down 1.3% and SOL down 1.5%, while CoinMarketCap's charts page showed all three up. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear, read at about 12:00 UTC: Alternative.me's index 10 (Extreme Fear), CoinGecko's own index 21 (Extreme Fear, from 27 yesterday); CoinMarketCap's index showed 12 out of 100. They are different indexes, so the numbers do not match.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips back to about $64,000 after a $2B weekend flush
stories.summary: Bitcoin bounced from its Sunday low near $62,000 but slid again on Monday, and has now fallen six weeks in a row. About $2B of bets made with borrowed money were force-closed over the weekend. That kind of selling has calmed down for now, and traders betting on a fall are now the ones paying to hold their positions.
points: Bitcoin was around $64,300, down 1.6% since midnight UTC, per CoinDesk at 11:03 UTC; Cointelegraph put it near $64,500.
The weekend low was $62,100, the lowest since 14 July, per CoinDesk; Cointelegraph says $61,950 on Bitstamp.
About $2B of positions were liquidated (force-closed) over the weekend, mostly bets on a rise, and liquidations in the latest 24 hours fell to $176M, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin is below its 200-week average, a long-term trend line, which Cointelegraph puts at $68,186.
The most-traded bitcoin options expire on 27 November; the biggest bets on a fall are at $50,000, $52,000 and $58,000, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Rates week: Warsh speaks at noon ET as traders price in a December hike; ETF outflows hit seven days
stories.summary: Fed Chair Warsh gives opening remarks at a San Francisco Fed conference today. Futures traders see a December interest-rate rise as close to certain; that is a market bet, not a Fed decision. Higher rates pull money away from risky assets like crypto. US spot bitcoin ETFs have had seven straight days of withdrawals.
points: CME FedWatch odds for a December hike are put at 92% for a 0.25-point rise and 8% for 0.5 points by KuCoin, and at 100% by the Motley Fool using data as of 12 November.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $185M on Friday 13 November, their seventh straight day of outflows, about $1.91B in total, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin ETFs lost about $829M for the week and about $2.1B so far in November, per Decrypt.
Ether ETFs took in $2.3M on Friday, ending a six-day outflow streak, but lost $336M for the week, per Decrypt.
Also this week: US retail sales Tuesday, Nvidia results Tuesday after the close and Fed minutes Wednesday, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Binance still restoring withdrawals after its $6.3B hack; Arbitrum vote on frozen funds ends today
stories.summary: The world's largest crypto exchange is still reopening withdrawals after the 29 October hack. It has reopened 87 networks and aims to reopen the rest this week; that is a target, not a guarantee. Arbitrum's community is voting on whether to hand frozen stolen funds back to Binance.
points: Binance reopened withdrawals on 87 networks, per Bitcoin.com News.
About $6.3B was stolen, including about 167,464 ETH and about $1.6B of USDT, and about $3B was reportedly frozen by third parties, per Bitcoin.com News.
An Arbitrum DAO vote on returning 8,425.997 ETH and 74,559,805.2 ARB to Binance for user losses, conditional on legal protection, ends 16 November, per CoinDesk.
Until withdrawals reopen, coins on the affected networks stay on the exchange; ignore anyone offering paid or faster withdrawals.

briefs.title: Russia opens crypto to ordinary investors
briefs.summary: Bank of Russia rules taking effect 17 November let non-qualified retail investors buy BTC, ETH and USDT up to an annual cap, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Crypto bill stalled; new SEC and CFTC picks
briefs.summary: The CLARITY market-structure bill is stalled after a failed 49-50 Senate vote on 15 September; Trump nominated Levine and Johnson to the SEC and Anonick and Rowland to the CFTC on 12 November, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Bitcoin miners hijacked at Luxor
briefs.summary: Attackers redirected mining power from just over a dozen customer accounts and collected about 0.243 BTC; Luxor patched the hole within 2 hours and will reimburse customers, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: JPMorgan and DBS link tokenized deposits
briefs.summary: The banks launched 24/7 instant transfers of tokenized US dollar deposits between the US and Singapore, with Ant International as the first client, per The Block.

briefs.title: Upbit owner swings to a loss
briefs.summary: Dunamu posted a Q3 net loss of 18.6B won (about $13.8M) and revenue fell 60.7%, a sign of how much trading has cooled, per The Block.

briefs.title: Vitalik backs higher fees for new accounts
briefs.summary: Buterin supports EIP-8037 for Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade, raising the gas cost of creating a new account from 36,600 to 197,900, per The Block.

briefs.title: Cardano holders reject a copper purchase
briefs.summary: A proposal to spend 22M ADA (about $5M) of treasury funds, about two-thirds of it on physical copper, was voted down, per CoinDesk.
